evals.prompt: Create a secure GitHub Actions CI workflow for a Node repo. It should run on pull requests and main branch pushes, install from package-lock.json, run npm test, and avoid giving secrets to forked PRs.
evals.expected_output: A GitHub Actions workflow with safe triggers, explicit read-only permissions, pinned actions, npm ci/test, timeout, concurrency, and no secret exposure to forked PRs.
expectations: The workflow uses pull_request rather than pull_request_target for PR CI.
The workflow sets contents: read or narrower permissions.
The job has timeout-minutes and dependency installation uses npm ci.
External action references include explicit versions or SHAs.
The response includes a validation command.

evals.prompt: Add a manual production deployment workflow using GitHub Actions environments and OIDC. It should not use static cloud credentials and should require production approval.
evals.expected_output: A manual environment-gated deployment with job-scoped OIDC permissions, serialized concurrency, pinned actions, and documented GitHub Environment reviewer configuration.
expectations: The workflow uses workflow_dispatch and a production environment.
Only the deploy job grants id-token: write.
The design does not require long-lived cloud access keys.
Privileged external actions are full-SHA pinned or the limitation is explicitly called out.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied release workflow for unsafe GitHub Actions patterns and propose a corrected design.
evals.expected_output: An audit of the supplied workflow that identifies privileged PR execution, overbroad permissions, mutable reusable-workflow refs, and unsafe event-text interpolation, then proposes safer trust boundaries.
expectations: The response flags pull_request_target combined with untrusted checkout or execution.
The response replaces permissions: write-all with narrow job permissions.
The response flags the reusable workflow reference at main as mutable.
The response flags direct issue-comment interpolation into run as shell-injection risk.
The corrected design separates untrusted validation from trusted publishing.
